Hi Jane / Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap here so we have alignment on pain, goals, and an actionable pilot outline. I tried to keep the numbers conservative — see attached cost model for the sensitivity table.

What we heard (pain points)
- Unpredictable per-request cost across peaks; current vendor billing spikes on tokens and network throughput.
- Tight budget for Q1: procurement target is ~USD 30k–45k for evaluation + initial pilot.
- Latency tail (p95) causes bad UX during shopping flows; needs p95 under ~300ms for page-driven prompts.
- Regressions from large-context requests (key-value cache cold starts) — want caching + batching to reduce duplicate token compute.

Key numbers you shared
- Baseline traffic: ~1.1B tokens/month (combined prompts + completions)
- Median request size: ~420 tokens; peak/session long-form sequences ~2,200 tokens (rare)
- Current average concurrency: 35 rps, burst to 240 rps during promos
- Target production SLA: p95 < 300ms, throughput support to 300 rps during short bursts

Redwood high-level TCO levers (summary)
- Token economics: we model input+output tokens. With batching and prefix cache, effective billed tokens can drop ~12–22% depending on hit rate.
- Batching: continuous batching on the serving runtime reduces per-token compute. For your workload we estimate a 15% CPU/GPU cost reduction at steady-state and larger wins at medium burst sizes.
- KV/prefix caching: for repeated user context (shopping carts, product prompts) conservatively assume a 10% token avoidance initially; engineering tune-up can push that higher.
- Quantization & model variant routing: using 8-bit quantized variants for lower-cost routes on lower-fidelity endpoints; we estimate an additional 8–12% token-cost-equivalent savings on background tasks.

Preliminary cost comparison (high level) — monthly estimate
- Current vendor: ~USD 18,000–24,000 (your provided billing)
- Redwood projected (baseline pilot configuration, conservative): ~USD 11,500–15,000
- Expected incremental savings range: USD 6k–9k/month (sensitivity in attached workbook)

Pilot options we recommend (pick one)
1) Focused eval (6 weeks) — objective: validate token savings + latency on production-like traffic
   - Committed throughput: 100 rps baseline, burst to 300 rps for 10s windows
   - Success metrics: p95 < 350ms by week 3, token reduction >=10% vs baseline by week 5
   - Budget: commit USD 18k for 6 weeks (includes reserved capacity + on-call support)

2) Production-sim pilot (8 weeks, heavier) — objective: prove scaling + cost model at near-production load
   - Committed throughput: 250 rps baseline, burst to 500 rps for 30s windows
   - Success metrics: p95 < 300ms, token reduction >=15%, validated fallback routing
   - Budget: commit USD 42k for 8 weeks (reserved capacity + SRE support + extended observability)

Immediate next steps (what I need from Finova)
- Confirm preferred pilot option (1 or 2) and target start week (we can start as early as Dec 20).
- Provide a short sample of 2–3 anonymized prompt flows (we'll need them for cache hit estimates).
- Procurement point-of-contact and any required clause redlines for our SOW.

What Redwood will deliver
- Short SOW + pricing addendum for the chosen pilot (48–72 hours)
- A pilot cost workbook (attached) with sensitivity toggles for batch size, cache hit, and model variants
- Dedicated SE time (Marissa) to run workload profiling and recommended runtime knobs

Attachments: finova_pilot_cost_model.xlsx (sensitivity tabs: baseline / optimistic / conservative)

Thanks — I'll follow up with a formal SOW once you pick an option. Looping Marissa for the technical deep-dive and Vivek for contract/discount conversations.
